questions.q: What is the correct order of operations in this capstone's design?
options: ServiceNow polls Meridian HR every few minutes for new hires
Meridian HR sends the full employee record directly inside the webhook
Meridian HR sends a thin webhook with just the employeeId, then ServiceNow calls back out via a REST Message to pull the full record
ServiceNow creates the sys_user first, then confirms the data with Meridian HR afterward
questions.explain: The webhook only notifies ServiceNow that something happened; the REST Message pull afterward retrieves the authoritative employee data.

questions.q: Looking at the webhook payload Meridian HR sends (employeeId, eventType, timestamp), what's notably absent that forces ServiceNow to make a follow-up call?
options: The timestamp field
The eventType field
An authentication header
The actual employee details — name, email, start date, department, manager
questions.explain: The webhook is deliberately thin — it carries only enough to identify who changed, not the authoritative data itself.

questions.q: Why is this integration classified as event-driven and inbound rather than polling?
options: Because Meridian HR can initiate contact itself the instant a new hire is created, instead of ServiceNow asking on a schedule
Because ServiceNow has no REST Message capability
Because polling is technically impossible against Meridian HR's API
Because event-driven integrations never need authentication
questions.explain: Event-driven means the other system calls in the moment something happens; polling would waste calls and delay same-day task creation.

questions.q: Why does this integration NOT need a MID Server?
options: MID Servers are never needed for HR integrations
Meridian HR is a cloud SaaS product with a public HTTPS API that ServiceNow's cloud can reach directly, with nothing behind a firewall
MID Servers only work with SOAP, not REST
The integration doesn't use any authentication
questions.explain: A MID Server closes the gap to systems with no public endpoint; Meridian HR's public API has no such gap to close.

questions.q: In the preview code `gs.info('Onboarding webhook received for employeeId: ' + payload.employeeId);`, what does this line actually accomplish?
options: It creates the pending sys_user record
It pulls the full employee record from Meridian HR
It logs that the notification arrived — a checkpoint, not the data pull itself
It authenticates the inbound request
questions.explain: This is just a logging checkpoint confirming the webhook was received; the actual pull is built in Lesson 27.
